goal: Every production build reports its seconds and its peak memory in the summary of the run that deployed it, a run goes red when the peak passes the median of the last ten production builds plus 10% or 75% of the machine, and the peak is at 75% of its machine or less: by the two free source-map switches on Vercel's 8 GB machine, or, only if they are not enough, by building in CI and deploying the prebuilt output. No paid machine, plan or add-on is used.
why: Today the build peaks at about 7.2 GB of Vercel's 8 GB (90%), was killed once on 11 November, and prints neither figure. After: ten production builds in a row peak at 6.0 GB or less (75%), and growth of a tenth turns a run red long before the wall.

depends_on.why: it measures both source-map switches under an 8 GB cap and writes their rows into docs/build-memory.md, which decide whether this step ends at stage 1; it also makes scripts/next-build.mjs print seconds and peak, which commit 1 here builds on
only for stage 2: it takes three type checks out of every push, so one more build in CI does not raise a push's runner-minutes

commits.title: Every production build reports its seconds and peak memory, and the deploy's wait prints them

changes.how: Plain Node ESM, no dependency. Export: median(numbers) (the middle of the sorted list, the mean of the two middle ones for an even count, null for an empty list); machineKb(meminfoText, cgroupMaxText) = MemTotal, or the smaller of it and cgroupMaxText/1024 when that text is a number (not 'max'); ceilingKb({ machineKb, history }) = the smaller of 0.75 * machineKb and, when history has at least 5 numbers, 1.10 * median(history); and buildVerdict({ peakKb, machineKb, history }) returning { ceilingKb, over: boolean, line: string } where line reads like 'Build: 263 s, peak 5.4 GB of 8.0 GB; ceiling 5.9 GB (median of the last 10 builds plus 10%, never above 75% of the machine)'. GB here is KB / 1048576 with one decimal. No sampler and no usedKb here: the peak is measured by step 1.20's startPeakSampler() in scripts/lib/peak-memory.mjs. history is the peaks of earlier production builds, newest last, the build being judged not among them.

Step 1.20 has already rewritten this file: it spawns `next build` with spawn (the 7 GB heap rule unchanged), starts `startPeakSampler()` from ./lib/peak-memory.mjs before spawning, and on the child's 'close' stops it, prints one line 'Build: <seconds> s, peak memory <x.x> GB (<source>)', appends that line to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set, writes BUILD_REPORT when set, and exits with next's code; an 'error' handler prints the line and exits 1. Keep all of that unchanged, the printed line's words included (1.20's recorder and docs read it), and add no second sampler. Add only: (1) Before spawning: read production's record of earlier builds: when process.env.VERCEL_ENV is 'production' or process.env.BUILD_STATS_FROM is set, `await fetch((process.env.BUILD_STATS_FROM || 'https://kaizenaflow.com') + '/api/health', { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) })` inside a try (the file is ESM, top-level await is allowed), and take `[...(Array.isArray(body.build?.history) ? body.build.history : []), ...(typeof body.build?.peakKb === 'number' && body.build.peakKb > 0 ? [body.build.peakKb] : [])].filter((n) => typeof n === 'number').slice(-10)` as history; on any failure history is []. Then write build-stats.json in the repository root (path.join(import.meta.dirname, '..', 'build-stats.json')) with JSON `{ commit, seconds: 0, peakKb: 0, machineKb: 0, history }` so the file exists while next traces the health route; commit is process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA || process.env.GITHUB_SHA || null. (2) In the 'close' handler, after 1.20's line is printed and only when the code is 0, overwrite build-stats.json with `{ commit, seconds: <the same seconds the line printed>, peakKb: peakBytes === null ? 0 : Math.round(peakBytes / 1024), machineKb: machineKb(<text of /proc/meminfo>, <text of /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max>), history }`, each file read with readFileSync in its own try (machineKb 0 when /proc/meminfo cannot be read; the cgroup text null when its file cannot be read). machineKb comes from ./lib/build-stats.mjs. Do not make the build fail on the peak: the verdict is the deploy job's (commit 3).

In outputFileTracingIncludes add one entry, with a comment that the build writes this file when it ends (scripts/next-build.mjs) and the health route reads it: "/api/health": ["./build-stats.json"]. Change nothing else in this commit.
Under the '# next.js' block add the line '/build-stats.json'.

Add to HealthReport: build: { seconds: number; peakKb: number; machineKb: number; history: number[] } | null, with a doc comment (the build that made this deployment: its seconds, its peak memory and the peaks of the ten builds before it; no secret). Add to checkHealth's deps: build?: HealthReport['build']; buildCommit?: string | null. Return build: deps.build ?? null. Change the commit line to: const commit = deps.commit ?? process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA ?? deps.buildCommit ?? null (a prebuilt deployment has no VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA; the build then wrote the commit itself). Export a pure parser readBuildStats(text: string): { build: HealthReport['build']; commit: string | null } that JSON-parses in a try and returns { build: null, commit: null } for anything that is not an object with a number seconds above 0 and a number peakKb; history is filtered to finite numbers and cut to the last 10.

Before calling checkHealth read the file: const stats = readBuildStats(await readFile(path.join(process.cwd(), 'build-stats.json'), 'utf8').catch(() => '')), with readFile from node:fs/promises, and pass build: stats.build and buildCommit: stats.commit. Keep connection(), the status code and the no-store header.

Change reportedCommit(url) into reportedHealth(url) returning { commit, build } from the same request (commit null and build null on any failure) and use .commit where the commit was used. After the line that prints 'Production runs ...' and before the smoke checks: when last.build is an object, compute buildVerdict({ peakKb: build.peakKb, machineKb: build.machineKb, history: build.history }) from './lib/build-stats.mjs', console.log its line, and when process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is set append '### Production build

' + line + '
' to that file with appendFileSync. When build is null print 'This deployment reports no build figures.' Do not exit on the verdict in this commit. Export buildVerdict's use as a small pure function buildLines(build) so the test can call it. Update the header comment.

Vitest, importing from '../../scripts/lib/build-stats.mjs' as src/lib/await-deploy.test.ts imports its script. Cases: median of [3,1,2] is 2 and of [] is null; machineKb with cgroup text '4294967296' is 4194304 and with 'max' is MemTotal; ceilingKb with machineKb 8388608 and ten history values of 5000000 is 5500000; with history of 7000000 it is 6291456 (the 75% line wins); with 3 history values it is the 75% line; buildVerdict for a peak 12% above the median and under 75% (peak 5600000, history ten times 5000000, machine 8388608) has over true; for a peak 5% above it has over false.

Add cases: checkHealth({ ...the file's usual stubs, build: { seconds: 263, peakKb: 5000000, machineKb: 8388608, history: [1] } }) reports that build; with no VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA (pass commit undefined and stub the env as the file's other cases do) and buildCommit 'abc' the commit is 'abc'; readBuildStats('not json') and readBuildStats('{"seconds":0,"peakKb":0}') give build null; a valid text gives the numbers and at most 10 history entries.
Add a case for buildLines(): a build object gives one line that starts 'Build: ' and names the ceiling; null gives the 'reports no build figures' line. Keep every existing case.

Under '## Watch' add a short part 'What every build reports': the file build-stats.json, how the peak is read (machine memory in use, sampled each second; the cgroup's own peak where there is one), that /api/health carries it with the ten builds before, and that the run's summary shows it. Add at the top of '## Watch', replacing the two bullets that name the Enhanced build machine: 'No paid build machine, plan or add-on is used, now or later (the owner, bloat review step 1.21). If the build needs room: the two source-map switches below, then the build in CI deployed prebuilt.' Also reword the last sentence of the 11 November note the same way. Lines at most 130 characters.
